deviation_mechanism: The physical discrepancy arises from the relationship between optical path length and physical thickness in thin-film stacks. The expected 375-385 nm band likely assumed a lower effective refractive index for layer 15 or an idealized quarter-wave condition at a different central wavelength. In reality, the local effective index at layer 15's spectral position is higher, compressing the required physical thickness (d = λ / 4n_eff). Additionally, cumulative phase shifts from adjacent higher-index layers create constructive/destructive interference patterns that reward thinner low-index spacing layers. The optimizer reduced layer 15 to ~220-265 nm to compensate for these phase accumulations and match the target transmission/reflection envelope, overriding the geometric initialization prior.
